captureContract.fingerprint: sha256 of a declared deterministic encoding of the exact returned/canonical value. Preserve null, missing and empty as distinct values; apply the same declared field projection/snippet bound on the independent canonical value.
captureContract.revision: Use an actual independently captured canonical/provider revision. A content hash binds a value but alone does not establish revision order, provider currentness or authority.
captureContract.epoch: Host-resolved current authorization/binding components. Capture both candidate-time and independent canonical-time snapshots; no epoch accepted from query text or the candidate payload.
captureContract.zeroAge: The frozen maxAgeMs and maxFutureSkewMs are both zero. Preserve actual measured clock values; do not round, copy responseAtMs into canonical.readAtMs or widen the policy to obtain current. If the actual read cannot meet it, record stale/unknown.
captureContract.directSql: Even when canonical content is selected directly by SQL, retain the actual candidate observation and independent trusted canonical validation. Do not duplicate a returned object as purported independent proof.
captureContract.authorization: onUnknown:degrade is a freshness disposition only. It never authorizes retaining a row after access is revoked.
captureContract.missingEvidence: Store null/unknown with the missing evidence reason. Do not replace unavailable canonical/provider proof with occurredAt, updated_at, cache time or an envelope timestamp.

controls.procedure: Read a controlled eligible entity through the real entrypoint and independently read the same canonical field under the current trusted scope. Bind returned/candidate/canonical versions and the actual request/response clocks.
controls.expected: current/accept only when every frozen boundary is satisfied; keep unknown or stale otherwise

controls.procedure: Commit a new canonical field value while retaining an old candidate or one old hydrated field. Preserve the row id and fresh envelope.
controls.expected: stale/degrade for the mismatched field; another fresh field cannot validate it

controls.procedure: Replay a recorded old field value with a freshly generated response/envelope clock and unchanged claimed applied status.
controls.expected: the returned value fingerprint fails currentness; envelope time never substitutes for a field witness

controls.procedure: Make the real candidate source revision differ from an independent current canonical revision while retaining an eligible entity.
Fail or refuse the independent canonical read without changing the returned candidate value.
controls.expected: unknown/degrade, never current; respect separate access refusals

controls.procedure: Omit one field revision, index/candidate revision, authority epoch or trusted observation clock from the capture.
controls.expected: unknown/degrade; no synthetic timestamps, revisions or epochs

controls.procedure: Inject a controlled rollback in the capture clock so responseAtMs precedes requestStartedAtMs.
controls.expected: not current; retain the invalid-clock evidence

controls.procedure: Set a controlled candidate/canonical observation beyond the frozen maxFutureSkewMs, retaining the original field value and identity.
controls.expected: not current; do not silently clamp to response time

controls.procedure: Replay canonical evidence collected before the real request and preserve an otherwise fresh envelope.
Capture a result, change the actual applicable grant/mapping/ACL/presence/config or privacy epoch, and replay the recorded candidate with a fresh cache clock.
controls.expected: previous epoch cannot validate currentness; revoked access yields no protected row/snippet/count/reference

controls.procedure: Commit a new eligible matching document or newly eligible field, query the actual reader/index paths before and after index visibility, and compare the known controlled corpus to returned candidates.
controls.expected: record omissions separately from freshness; hydration of returned rows cannot discharge candidate coverage

controls.procedure: Change the canonical privacy rule or reader set between controlled captures and compare the delivered label/disclosure ledger with the current rule.
controls.expected: labels and restricted disclosures reflect the authorized delivery; old privacy proof cannot certify a new epoch

controls.procedure: Hold one real-adapter provider response, let another settle, then revoke or change the fast source's mapped identity/config/binding or grant before the slow response settles.
controls.expected: post-settlement liveSearchBindingCurrent/currentAuth rejects old binding or grant; no revoked hit or disclosure is delivered

controls.procedure: Execute the sealed candidate/decrypt/rank/merge path on controlled versioned content; compare each opened returned field with an independent authorized canonical opening, including a stale-field variant.
controls.expected: sealing/key success alone does not validate content revision; mixed/old plaintext remains stale or unknown

controls.procedure: Exercise an actual timed-out leg and total deadline through documents:search; bind empty/partial output, leg report and all output references to the captured request.
controls.expected: timeout/partial stays explicit; no currentness witness is manufactured for an absent or failed leg

observations: All four leg rows receive a scope discriminator from documents:search after the dedicated reader returns.

Personal rows also receive privacy from discloseDocuments although personal privacy is outside the three frozen personal field policies; capture that key in the output census without silently treating it as a newly qualified policy.
A direct local DB read can bind imported content to the stored version. It does not establish that an upstream provider has no newer version.
Live provider responses are followed by binding and grant rechecks after all providers settle. This is a source observation, not an executed recurrence or provider-current witness.
The registered live-search integration suite uses a controlled fake provider. Its native receipts can prove only that adapter/custody scenario, never a production provider's content revision.
executionPrerequisites: Use the existing canonical isolated Postgres test/fixture surfaces; do not seed private production corpus rows.
Predeclare exact field/path/control/corpus/config identities before execution and retain attempted, executed, judged and failed/unknown partitions.
Recheck source bytes against every pin immediately before execution and commit the actual source used in evidence.
Do not rerun R10 retrieval, historical inventory tests or paid judge attempts solely to reconstruct saved proof.
Provider content currentness requires an admissible provider revision/clock capture; missing capability remains unknown.
P-001 qualified labels, cost/budget population, runtime closure, independent acceptance and shipment remain separate open requirements.
